text:
Elaine: Quick sync: UX review for pipeline form. Two outstanding debates: 1) how to surface async validation (duplicate dataset name / reserved words) 1 inline optimistic errors vs summary-on-submit? 2) rollback/restore destructive flows 1 typed-confirm or undoable soft-delete? Thoughts?

Sam: For async checks (name exists) I prefer inline non-blocking hint that updates after debounce: "Name already taken (change to continue)". Only block on submit if backend rejects. Keeps typing flow smooth. :clock1: 

Priya: Inline hint is fine but we need to avoid flicker when debounce triggers. Show spinner in-field while checking and only render error after server says duplicate.

Courtney: Summary-on-submit is helpful for discoverability on long forms. My vote: inline for field-specific & immediate checks, but always show a short summary after a failed submit with anchors to each invalid field. Summary appears only after submit attempt.

morgan: Accessibility: for inline async errors use role="status" messages tied to aria-describedby. If you show spinner, make sure it's aria-hidden and announce the result when complete. Avoid duplicate messages between inline and summary (use slightly different phrasing).

Alex: Copy suggestion: inline async message: "Name in use 1 choose a different name or add a suffix." Summary entry: "Name: already in use (opens field)." Link should focus the input and put cursor at end.

Sam: Also we should decide debounce timing. 400ms felt decent in prototypes. Too short -> server spam, too long -> poor UX. 400-500ms range I recommend.

Elaine: Good notes. Now rollback/restore: our current modal asks "Are you sure you want to rollback to v1?" That's vague. Options: A) typed-confirm for irreversible rollbacks, B) soft-rollback + toast with undo for reversible operations.

Priya: If backend supports snapshot restore, prefer soft-rollback with undo visible for 30s. Only use typed-confirm when operation destroys data (e.g., purge logs).

morgan: Accessibility + copy: avoid color-only cues in the modal. Use icon + clear paragraph describing effect: "Restores model config to v1. This will stop current runs and cannot be undone if you select 'permanent rollback'." If typed-confirm required, instruct user exactly what to type and set focus to input.

Courtney: UX pattern: show two-step toggle in modal: radio "soft rollback (undoable)" vs "permanent rollback (typed confirm required)". That surface product intent and reduces accidental selection.

Alex: Need aria patterns: modal role="dialog" aria-modal="true"; if typed-confirm input present, set aria-describedby to include the typed instructions and use aria-live="polite" for any result messages. Ensure focus trap and return focus on close.

Elaine: Action items: Sam to prototype debounce + inline spinner copy, Priya to validate backend undo window, Courtney to wire summary-on-submit anchor behavior, Alex/morgan to add aria snippets and typed-confirm pattern examples. I'll pull a quick Figma with both modal variants tonight and tag y'all.

aria-bot: A11y reminder: expose error text via aria-describedby, ensure announcement on async completion, don't rely on color only, and test with NVDA/VoiceOver.
